language_task: Put the spoon in the drawer.
outcome_evidence: The robot approaches the spoon and lowers its gripper beside the handle at frames 70–86 in image, left_ego_image and wrist_image. It then withdraws empty at frames 87–101 while the spoon remains on the tabletop. At frame 116, image and left_ego_image still show the spoon outside the drawer, establishing a failed acquisition rather than merely an unconfirmed placement.

failure_annotations.explanation: Following the near-handle acquisition attempt at frames 76–86, the gripper begins withdrawing without the spoon at frame 87. Frames 90–101 in left_ego_image and wrist_image show increasing separation while the spoon stays on the table; image and left_ego_image confirm it remains there through frame 116. The attempted acquisition therefore fails to advance the spoon toward the drawer; the underlying cause is not visible.
failure_annotations.recovery: Reposition the open gripper so its fingers straddle the spoon handle, lower carefully, close and verify possession with a small lift before transporting it into the open drawer; no human intervention is visibly needed.
failure_annotations.severity_evidence: The spoon remains on the tabletop, with no visible damage, dropped object or disruption to surrounding objects.
failure_annotations.resetability_evidence: The spoon remains accessible in its original tabletop area, so another acquisition attempt requires no environmental reset or human intervention.
